learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Volume Conduction.
Apply Volume Conduction to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Electrical fields spread through cerebrospinal fluid, skull and skin before reaching electrodes. Each sensor therefore samples a mixture of sources.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Volume conduction blurs spatial localisation and inflates zero-lag similarity between channels. Source modelling can reduce ambiguity but depends on modelling assumptions and signal quality.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: This explains why topographic colour does not equal a sharply bounded cortical lesion and why connectivity metrics require caution.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Treating neighbouring electrodes as independent brain regions can exaggerate localisation and connectivity claims.

Treat statistical rarity as proof of disorder

reviewPrompts.answer: Volume conduction blurs spatial localisation and inflates zero-lag similarity between channels. Source modelling can reduce ambiguity but depends on modelling assumptions and signal quality.
This explains why topographic colour does not equal a sharply bounded cortical lesion and why connectivity metrics require caution.
Treating neighbouring electrodes as independent brain regions can exaggerate localisation and connectivity claims.
A scalp maximum is a clue to a field, not a GPS coordinate.
